headline: Highest risk is medium: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots/clipboard while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list, so direct pairwise harm is limited but leakage and misinterpretation remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a docs-only, non-runnable list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject ChatGPT Desktop. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste into ChatGPT Desktop’s clipboard/files/screen-capture inputs, which makes prompt injection possible but unusual and user-mediated. Both agents are cited because the pathway requires content from A and ingestion by B.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is manually copied into ChatGPT Desktop or uploaded as a file, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to interpret pasted repository text as instructions, THEN attacker-controlled text can influence outputs.
mitigations: Avoid pasting untrusted list entries into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before copy-paste.
Review pasted content as data, not instructions.
Disable clipboard-based workflows for this task.
requires-engineering: add provenance labeling for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and files from supported macOS apps, while awesome-nlp itself exposes no data. The pairwise risk is that sensitive material from B’s inputs can be surfaced in outputs or sent to vendor APIs, especially if the user mixes local files with the docs-only A content. A is cited for lack of intrinsic data, B for the actual leakage surface.
conditions: IF the operator uploads sensitive files or screenshots into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN those contents may be exposed in generated outputs.
IF files from supported macOS apps are read into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN local workspace data can enter the model context.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive files to ChatGPT Desktop.
Use redacted copies for any analysis.
Close unrelated documents before enabling app access.
Restrict clipboard use during sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive work into a separate environment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, shell, or network capabilities and is not runnable, while ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write path between the pair, so a capability conflict is provably blocked by the profiles. Both agents are cited to show the absence of conflicting writes.
conditions: IF agent_a gains a writable runtime or agent_b gains filesystem or git write access, THEN conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a static reference list.
Do not grant agent_b filesystem write permissions.
Avoid using shared git worktrees for this pair.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can treat pasted or file-derived content as context and then generate downstream actions or advice, while awesome-nlp is a static NLP resource list that may be used as source material. If B relies on A’s content without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect recommendations or actions. Both agents are relevant because A supplies the source material and B consumes it.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp entries are pasted into ChatGPT Desktop as authoritative source text, THEN B may propagate errors without verification.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to draft actions from A-derived content, THEN downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Verify A-derived claims against primary sources.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite and cross-check before acting.
Separate summarization from decision-making.
Mark awesome-nlp as non-authoritative reference material.
requires-engineering: add automated source verification.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced for awesome-nlp, and ChatGPT Desktop’s documented data classes are general user content rather than regulated data. The only plausible compliance issue is if the operator places regulated material into B, but that is not shown here. A is cited for lack of sensitive data classes; B is cited for the handling surface.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is entered into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN compliance review is required.
IF the operator relies on ChatGPT Desktop for retention-sensitive workflows, THEN policy mismatch must be checked.
mitigations: Do not enter regulated data into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use de-identified samples only.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Review vendor policy for the specific data class.
requires-engineering: route regulated workflows to a compliant environment.
